MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The stainless self-tapping screws fit my repeated purchases of fasteners for practical assembly work, especially wood and sheet-metal projects.",
    "Flap discs make sense after cutting wheels because smoothing cut edges is a natural next step, provided the discs fit my grinder.",
    "Brass rods fit small fabrication work supported by my metal drill bits and caliper, while disposable gloves would be useful for the adhesive and epoxy work in my history."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The filaments and UV printer resin require compatible printers and a printing project, neither of which my purchases establish. Tabletop epoxy serves a different purpose from printer resin.",
    "Adhesive tape does not give me a reason to buy expanding-foam gun cleaner; that cleaner depends on a specific tool and material I have not shown a need for.",
    "The foam roll and emergency switch could support particular projects, but I have no current padding, soundproofing, or electrical-control need that would make me choose them."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My interest in hands-on fabrication seems to have been stretched into an assumed interest in 3D printing.",
    "Shared words such as resin, adhesive, and DIY seem to count too much when the materials have different uses and equipment requirements."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My repeated fastener purchases make practical joining and assembly supplies more compelling than materials with only a broad project connection.",
    "The connection between successive tasks matters to me: cutting metal creates a plausible need for edge finishing, while buying epoxy does not create a need for printer consumables.",
    "Tool compatibility, fastener dimensions, and a concrete use matter before I choose a specialized supply, even when its general purpose interests me."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations partly understood my fastening and fabrication work but extended that interest too far into specialized supplies without evidence of the required equipment or project."
}
